This is not a conformance claim: only the checks listed here ran. ### Findings 1. **img-alt** · SC 1.1.1 Non-text Content (A) · failure Element: `` (line 1) Affects: screen reader Problem: The image has no alt attribute, so a screen reader reads out the file name. Fix: ```diff - + ``` Note: if the image is only decorative, use `alt=""` instead. ### Needs a manual test - Keyboard only: press Tab through the whole page. Every control should be reachable, the order should follow the reading order, and focus should never get trapped (SC 2.1.1, 2.1.2, 2.4.3). - Screen reader pass (for example NVDA with Firefox, or VoiceOver with Safari): names, roles, states and headings should be read out as expected (SC 4.1.2, 1.3.1). - Voice control pass (for example Voice Control or Dragon): say each visible label and check that it activates the control (SC 2.5.3). - Zoom and reflow: set the browser to 200%, then to 400% at 1280 CSS px wide (about 320 CSS px). No content should be lost and nothing should need scrolling in two directions (SC 1.4.4, 1.4.10). - Alt text quality: the script only checks that alt text exists. A person must check that it says what each image is for (SC 1.1.1). ### Not checked here - Contrast, focus-ring style, spacing and target size: not checked; ui-polish owns them. - Whether the flow makes sense and whether the words are clear: not part of this audit. ### Open questions - What does `a.png` show?
